idiom_name: Task fan-out + linked CancellationTokenSource + try/finally scope (Task.WhenAll/WhenAny)
implementation_notes: .NET has no task-scope object, so the scope is a try/finally around awaited tasks: Task.WhenAll completes only after every child has completed, which makes the method body the join point. Children run as Task-returning methods with a token from CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource, so cancelling the parent also cancels them; for fail-fast behaviour await Task.WhenAny in a loop, Cancel() on the first fault, and then drain the rest with Task.WhenAll before leaving. Cancellation follows the cooperative model of managed threads - children must observe the token (ThrowIfCancellationRequested or polling).
pitfalls: Awaiting Task.WhenAll surfaces only the first exception; the remaining failures live in the aggregate Exception property and are easy to lose.
An async void child is not awaitable and escapes the scope entirely - every child must return Task or Task<T>.
Faulted children do not stop their siblings by themselves; without the linked token source (and children actually checking it) the scope waits for work nobody wants.
A child that swallows OperationCanceledException looks successful to the scope, so cancellation-aware catch blocks must rethrow.
